content.overview: Section 71 regulates issue of debentures, security, the debenture trustee, the debenture redemption reserve where applicable, and remedies on default.
content.glance: Section 71 regulates issue of debentures, security, the debenture trustee, the debenture redemption reserve where applicable, and remedies on default.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 71 (Debentures). Section 71 addresses convertible debentures, restrictions on voting rights, secured debentures and trustees, remedies for failure to redeem debentures or pay interest, and specific enforcement of a contract to take up and pay for debentures. Any debenture redemption reserve requirement must be determined from the current Act and applicable rules, including the company/instrument category, exemptions and issue date; do not assume a universal percentage. Current rule-level and case-law review remains open.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: A company may issue debentures with an option to convert, subject to the special-resolution and approval conditions in the section. An unsecured debenture issue to the public is constrained; secured debentures generally require creation of a charge and appointment of a debenture trustee. The trustee protects holders and may enforce security. Debentures do not ordinarily carry voting rights. Amounts are to be transferred to a debenture redemption reserve where the section and rules still require it; later rule changes on the reserve must be checked for the issue date. On failure to redeem or pay interest, the Tribunal may order redemption and, in a qualifying case, direct commencement of the insolvency process as the section provides. A contract to subscribe is specifically enforceable.

examples.title: Voting
examples.body: A plain debenture holder does not vote as a member merely by holding the debenture.

examples.title: Default
examples.body: Non-payment of interest can be taken to the Tribunal under s. 71.

hypotheticals.question: Must every company maintain a debenture redemption reserve at the same percentage?
hypotheticals.analysis: No universal percentage should be assumed. Check the current applicable rules, company and instrument category, exemptions and issue date.

hypotheticals.question: A company fails to redeem debentures at maturity. What must be analysed?
hypotheticals.analysis: Establish the maturity/default facts and apply the precise Tribunal powers and conditions in the current text of section 71.

distinctions: A debenture is a debt instrument under s. 71. A share is part of capital under ss 43-44. A deposit under ss 73-76 is a different acceptance-of-money regime.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every debenture issue has the same redemption-reserve requirement.
misconceptions.correction: Determine the requirement under current rules, category and applicable exemptions.

misconceptions.trap: Treating a debenture holder as a voting member merely because the holder is a creditor.
misconceptions.correction: A debenture does not by itself make its holder a member with voting rights.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Do debenture holders vote at general meetings?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Not by virtue of the debenture alone. Voting rights are a shareholder attribute unless a specific statutory or conversion event applies.
